$doc: THE SINGLE DEFINITION of which asset-frontmatter keys the DATABASE owns after Phase 1.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS AT ALL. On 2026-08-01 this one list lived in three hand-maintained
copies: DB_OWNED / DB_OWNED_REND in .claude/skills/content-status/scan.js, I9_FLAT / I9_REND
in scripts/content-engine/content-doctor.ts, and DB_OWNED_ASSET_KEYS / DB_OWNED_RENDITION_KEYS
in scripts/content-engine/content-sync.ts. They had ALREADY diverged on the day they were
written: the doctor was missing 'unipile_account' and 'thumb_confirmed', and the doctor is the
NIGHTLY AUTOMATED alarm while scan.js is hand-run, so the weaker list was the one nobody has to
remember to run. That is the exact defect Phase 1 exists to remove (two copies of one fact, one
of them updated, no alarm), reintroduced by Phase 1. Keith's ruling, 2026-08-01: consolidate,
and the strict superset wins.
WHY JSON, AND WHY HERE. scan.js is zero-dependency CommonJS run directly by `node`, not tsx,
and it lives under .claude/skills/, so it cannot import a TypeScript module out of the
frontend. JSON is the one format both sides load as a real BUILD-TIME import rather than by
re-parsing each other's source: scan.js does require('./db-owned-keys.json'), content-doctor.ts
does a resolveJsonModule import, and content-sync.ts re-exports the doctor's derivation. So
there are no copies to keep in sync, which is the only version of 'keep these in sync' that has
ever worked. It sits beside scan.js because scan.js is the consumer with no path arithmetic to
get wrong, and because content-doctor already resolves this directory for invariant 2.
WHY THE WHY IS A FIELD AND NOT A COMMENT. JSON has no comments, and this repo's rule is that a
comment records the incident behind the rule. So the reasons are 'why' strings, which has the
side benefit that a consumer can print them at the point of failure.
HOW TO READ AN ENTRY.
key        the frontmatter spelling a human once typed.
aliases    other spellings of the SAME fact that must also be refused. A fact copied back
under the database's own column name is the same second copy, better disguised.
column     the qualified column that owns the fact now, or null when nothing owns it.
ownerNote  appended in brackets after the column when a consumer names the owner.
retiredAs  the owner string used when column is null. Required exactly when column is null.
mirrored   true when content-sync's generated state block renders this fact, which is the
ONLY condition under which a stripper may delete the key from a file. A key
deleted from the file and absent from the mirror is a fact with nowhere left to
live: that is section 1's failure shape running backwards.
why        the incident or the reasoning, where it is not obvious.
ADDING A KEY. Add it here, in one place. A key may only take mirrored: true once a column
actually holds it AND renderStateBlock shows it: on 2026-08-01 approved_by / approved_date were
on the delete list with no column to move to, and stripping them would have deleted Keith's own
business approval into git history and out of every live store.

asset.why: Keith's BUSINESS approval to ship, a different act from Ewa's clinical sign-off. The column was added by 20260801_content_assets_business_approval.sql BEFORE this key was allowed to be stripped.
The column is deliberately NOT named after the frontmatter key it replaces, so a reader who transforms the name themselves gets it wrong. Hence the mapping is written out rather than derived.

The last real drift this pair caught: on 2026-07-31 the-stack and when-a-test-earns-its-place carried 2026-07-31 in frontmatter against 2026-07-09 in the database, and the FILE was right. Commit 5798f66 had rewritten both scripts and re-run the pre-flight, which found a HARD compliance hit the v1 copy had carried unflagged. The rule that caught it: never pick a winner, stop and report.
A non-empty ewa_task proves a question was ASKED, not answered. An EMPTY one is worse than a filled one, because it reads as 'no Ewa task' to anyone who trusts it.

asset.ownerNote: written only by the sign-off sync

rendition.why: The live post, and the single most useful cell for a human orienting in the repo. content-sync renders it as a sixth column the phase brief did not ask for, because a column the brief forgot is cheaper to add than a fact to recover.

Refused, but NOT on the stripper's delete list, and the two are different questions. The column exists, so the fact has a home; content-sync neither SELECTs it nor renders a cell for it, so deleting it from a file today would put it nowhere. No live asset file carries it. Give it a cell in renderStateBlock first, then flip this to true in the same edit.

rendition.retiredAs: nothing (retired: the thumbnail gate is in gate_rendition_publish())
rendition.why: The ancestor of this whole class: a boolean a human typed to assert a Drive fact nothing checked, read by the old scan.js G3. It never had a column and never should. It is watched forever so it can never be typed into a file again. content-doctor did NOT watch it before 2026-08-01, which is half of the divergence this file was created to end.
